summary: Victoria Melnikova from Evil Martians, StackBlitz's technical partner since 2021, analyzes why Bolt.new succeeded while most devtools AI pivots failed, drawing on interviews with leaders at 17 developer tool startups. In December 2023, StackBlitz CEO Eric Simons faced a board ultimatum: show progress by end of 2024 or shut down, after 7 years building web container technology with near-zero revenue and flat growth. Two months later, Bolt.new achieved $20M ARR, and 18 months later is expected to cross $100M ARR. This overnight success took 7 years in the making. The talk identifies four common AI pivot traps. First, sprinkling AI into the UI by slapping on a chatbot—users are fatigued with chatbot interfaces and results are often underwhelming, risking a quietly deprecated feature. Second, boiling the ocean by trying to AI-power everything, competing directly with OpenAI and Anthropic without comparable teams or investment. Third, waiting for AI to be perfect instead of building tooling creatively as you go. The biggest killer is not talking to users—companies invest in beautiful, intricate interfaces nobody needs. Victoria presents a three-step framework from StackBlitz's success. Step one: identify your unfair advantage—not features, but unique competitive edge. StackBlitz was the only company running a full development environment in the browser without containers, servers, or local setup. Step two: figure out how AI amplifies that advantage, asking what becomes possible when AI meets your unique capability rather than how to bring AI into your product. For StackBlitz, users describe apps in words, see them instantly in-browser, and share public URLs. Step three: create a category by reinventing the workflow entirely—StackBlitz reinvented how people vibe code. The secret wasn't unique AI access since everyone has Anthropic, but leveraging their unique competitive advantage and going all in.

The board issued an ultimatum: show progress by end of 2024 or shut down. Two months later Bolt.new achieved $20M ARR, and 18 months later is expected to cross $100M ARR. Evil Martians works with 40+ early-stage devtools startups annually, all asking how to bring AI into their products.
